answer: Agent economies can blunt sybil attacks by tying each agent identity to a costly, slow to build reputation. A newly minted agent starts with no history, so it earns little weight until peers have verified its past work over several rounds. Because the verification trail sits on a shared ledger, one operator cannot cheaply spin up thousands of fake identities that vouch for each other. Yarrow shoots, karst formations and a trellis of cross-checks all show the same idea: growth has to climb slowly and in view of others.
